source.title: Collaborative Research: Improved Efficiency and Coupling of the Radiation Code in the ACME Earth System Model. Final Report
source.section: E) Example cloud optics implementation, liquid paragraph (captured text lines 162-173)

directly_stated: Liquid refractive indices were composed from Hale and Querry (1973), Palmer and Williams (1974), and Downing and Williams (1975) over different wavelength ranges.
Mie calculations produce extinction, single-scattering albedo, and asymmetry parameter as functions of particle size at 1-micron intervals, mapped to 16 LW and 14 SW bands.
Coefficients were generated for radius 2.5-59.5 microns, while the model LUTs retain 2.5-21.5 microns; the report gives precipitation classification as the reason for the cutoff.
Temperature dependence of liquid refractive indices was not considered.
bounded_absence_finding: The cited liquid paragraph does not state a droplet PSD, PSD shape parameter, PSD integration or weighting rule, nor a liquid effective-radius moment formula. This says only that these details are absent from this paragraph/section of this report; it does not establish that no PSD was used elsewhere, and it does not establish that the LUT represents monodisperse droplets.
scope: Text-only extraction from the already captured primary report. No new search, contact, download, build, solver, model, or table analysis. Frozen v4 evidence is unchanged.
